correctness.rationale: With y_t=v_t/G² and s=1-beta2, the recurrence is y_t=y_{t-1}-s sign(y_{t-1}-1). Starting from zero, it advances by exactly s until it either lands on one or first overshoots. Integer reciprocal 1/s gives exact hitting and then sign zero freezes the state. Otherwise the first overshoot is exactly one step above the last subunit lattice point, and the next step returns to that point, forcing a two-cycle. The first moment and Adam comparison are elementary closed recurrences. The exact verifier checks locking cases, nonlocking cycles, cycle width and the reported parameter grid.

final_claim: For source-form Yogi with zero initial second moment and a constant nonzero gradient, the normalized second moment either reaches the target exactly and locks when 1/(1-beta2) is an integer, or enters a permanent two-cycle whose exact width is (1-beta2) times the squared gradient. The commonly reported beta2 values 0.9, 0.99 and 0.999 lie on the locking set.
